drafts.body:
Jermaine,

Good, and the honest answer to your question first: we do not have a pre-built list of associations facing federal action. We build it per client.

For Bridgepoint that would mean filtering on things we can actually observe: associations and companies with registered lobbying activity, recent rulemaking exposure in their sector, comment-period participation, new federal contracts, or a Washington office they do not yet have. Those signals get us to organisations likely to need representation. The email then does the qualifying, because the ones actually facing something reply.

Worth thirty minutes to decide which of those signals matter most for your practice:

• Tuesday, August 18 at 1:00 PM EDT
• Wednesday, August 19 at 1:30 PM EDT

drafts.lead: Don Hanna, I-Resource Group - would pay for results, burned by upfront spend before, wants process and what makes us different
drafts.body:
Don,

Straight answer on the money first, because it is the part that decides everything else. We charge a flat monthly retainer. We are not a pay-for-results shop, so if that is a hard requirement we are not your people and I would rather say it now than after a call.

Why: the moment we are paid per result, our incentive is volume and yours is arguing about what counted. You have already paid for that mistake once.

What is different is narrower than most claims. We run the outreach in your name from separate sending infrastructure, replies come to you directly, and if the targeting is wrong you will know inside two weeks because the wrong people will be replying. That is on us to fix, and it is visible rather than reported.

If that is worth twenty minutes:

• Tuesday, August 18 at 2:30 PM EDT
• Wednesday, August 19 at 1:30 PM EDT
• Monday, August 24 at 1:30 PM EDT

Taking the payment question first, since it decides whether the rest is worth reading.

We are paid from day one. Flat monthly retainer, not per meeting and not on results. The reason is that the first few weeks are infrastructure: domains, mailboxes, warming, list building. Nobody can do that on contingency and do it properly, and anyone offering to is either front-loading the cost elsewhere or planning to spray.

What you get for it: outreach running in your name from separate sending domains, replies landing directly with you, and targeting we adjust as we learn which segments actually respond.

Gagan,

Research conversations are a different job from selling, and worth being clear about.

We can target the people you want to learn from and get them replying to you. What changes is the message: an ask for twenty minutes of their thinking converts quite differently from a pitch, and usually better at this stage.

On cost and a trial, honestly: we are a flat monthly retainer and there is a few-week ramp while domains warm, so a very short trial tends to end right when it starts working. If you want something small, the sensible version is a narrow list and a single well-aimed campaign rather than a shortened one.

Worth twenty minutes to see whether that shape suits:
